deadline.note: Model assumption, not a forecast. A hazard node must be left before the earlier of the depth rule and the distance rule.

profiles.note: Synthetic shares of the estimated population. 'assisted' needs transport and is handed over outside task 03.

model.note: Logit stochastic user equilibrium solved by MSA, loaded in priority waves.
model.capacityNote: The graph gives nominal pedestrian flows of 300-900 people/h per road. An evacuation uses the full street width; Fruin's walkway capacity is about 4,500 people/h per metre, so the nominal values are scaled by 10. Calibrate before operational use.
model.bprNote: Above capacity the BPR curve continues along its tangent, which approximates queueing instead of diverging.
model.wavesNote: Waves are priority classes: each is assigned on the road and shelter capacity left by the more urgent ones. With a median free-flow reserve of about 9 minutes, delaying departures costs more than it relieves (Valencia: 64 % on time with 0 min stagger, 45 % with 5 min, 12 % with 10 min).
